correctness.rationale: For a hypothetical two-colouring, exact half-balance on every edge yields r_i+c_j-2x_ij=n-2. Summing by rows and columns forces r_i=c_i; unless n=4, all row sums are equal and then every off-diagonal x_ij is equal, contradicting n>=3. The n=4 witness is explicit. Three-colour witnesses are explicit for n=3,5, and for n>=6 the one-factorization construction has per-colour endpoint degree at most ceil((n-1)/3), giving every adjacent colour count at most n-2. The verifier independently checks the small cases and construction range.

value.rationale: Crown graphs are a canonical regular bipartite family and a one-factor deletion of K_{n,n}. The theorem completely determines a newly introduced colouring invariant on the family, exposes a unique exceptional order, and supplies a structural two-colour rigidity argument not provided by the broad minimum-degree upper bounds. The degree-4 crown Cr_5 also sits exactly below the published three-colour minimum-degree threshold, so its explicit three-colour resolution is mathematically informative rather than a routine parameter substitution.
